topic.seo_description: Explore RET fusion gene research in thyroid and lung cancers. Discover latest biomarker studies, diagnostic advances, and targeted treatment breakthroughs.
topic.seo_intro:
RET (REarranged during Transfection) gene fusions represent a significant breakthrough in cancer research, particularly in thyroid and lung cancers. When the RET gene undergoes rearrangement, it can create fusion proteins that drive cancer development and progression. These genetic alterations occur in a subset of patients and have become increasingly important targets for precision medicine approaches. Understanding RET fusions helps oncologists identify patients who may benefit from specific targeted therapies, potentially improving treatment outcomes and quality of life.

The study of RET as a biomarker has transformed how researchers and clinicians approach diagnosis and treatment selection. Advanced molecular testing can now detect RET fusions in tumor samples, enabling personalized treatment strategies. This discovery has led to the development of specialized RET-targeted drugs that work specifically against cancers driven by these mutations. For patients with RET-positive cancers, this precision approach offers hope for more effective treatments with potentially fewer side effects compared to traditional chemotherapy.

The research landscape surrounding RET continues to evolve rapidly, with ongoing clinical trials exploring new therapeutic combinations and patient populations. On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed studies, clinical trial data, and diagnostic advances in RET-driven cancer research. Our curated content represents current scientific findings to help patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals stay informed about this important area of cancer biology and treatment innovation.

articles.title: Discovery of CN-3 as a Next-Generation RET Inhibitor Potently Overcoming Multiple Mutations.
articles.hook: CN-3 RET inhibitor overcomes drug-resistant mutations in thyroid cancer
articles.summary: CN-3, a new RET inhibitor, effectively blocks multiple drug-resistant mutations in RET-driven cancers including medullary thyroid and lung cancer.

articles.title: FDA-approved RET protein-tyrosine kinase inhibitors in the management of RET-driven thyroid and lung cancer.
articles.hook: RET inhibitors improve outcomes in RET-driven thyroid and lung cancers
articles.summary: FDA-approved drugs targeting RET protein effectively treat thyroid and lung cancers driven by RET mutations or fusions.

articles.title: A Novel Approach to Targeting DLL3 with Tarlatamab in a Patient with Medullary Thyroid Carcinoma after Progression on Selpercatinib.
articles.hook: Tarlatamab targets DLL3 in selpercatinib-resistant medullary thyroid cancer
articles.summary: A new drug called tarlatamab shows promise for treating medullary thyroid cancer in patients who stop responding to previous treatments.

articles.title: First-line versus second-line use of selpercatinib in treatment of RET fusion-positive advanced non-small cell lung cancer: a cost-effectiveness analysis.
articles.summary: Using selpercatinib early in treatment is more cost-effective than delaying it for advanced lung cancer with RET mutations.

articles.title: Retreatment with First-Generation Selective RET Inhibitors in RET-Rearranged NSCLC Pretreated with Selpercatinib or Pralsetinib - Results from the RET-MAP Registry.
articles.summary: RET-rearranged lung cancer patients who relapsed after initial RET inhibitor treatment benefited from retreatment with the same drug class.

articles.title: Efficacy of selpercatinib as a first-line treatment for RET-fusion positive non-small-cell lung cancer: a novel two-stage Bayesian network meta-analysis.
articles.summary: Selpercatinib significantly improves survival outcomes compared to chemotherapy for RET-fusion positive lung cancer as first-line treatment.

articles.title: Real-world external control arm for the single-arm LIBRETTO-001 trial of selpercatinib in RET-mutation-positive medullary thyroid cancer: RECALIB-RET.
articles.summary: Selpercatinib outperformed standard treatments in real-world data for RET-mutated medullary thyroid cancer patients.

articles.summary: Researchers discovered that CCDC6-RET, a fusion protein driving lung and thyroid cancers, uniquely functions as a dual ATP- and ADP-dependent kinase with a novel self-activation mechanism.
